label: canon-c16-in12-n2
_why: THE COST-SLOPE SWEEP, BATCH 1 OF ~4 (user-ruled 2026-09-14: 'go on with the tests' - about 30 hours, four 2+1 batches, to find the sweet spot where world GDP does not diverge a lot from vanilla, the initial input increase is high enough to push rung 0's break-even output price up and ensure obsolescence, and capital is LESS abundant than vanilla - less depeasantation by 1936 in most majors; unified A and B; the early dip tolerated - 'realign with vanilla by the 1930s, do not drop dead (-70%) in 1836-1860, dropping 20% is OK'). THE DIAL is the building-cost slope C^era between FLAT (C 1: F110 at A 2.2 and the A 1.9 batch at 1.80x - the world doubles, rung 0 dies, pools hoard, workers per capita ABOVE vanilla) and A^era (C 2.2: canon-je24-a22-in12 at 0.65x - rung 0 alive at 57% staffed, the frontier scarce, prices 0.85x vanilla). This book: canon-je24-a22-in12 with building_cost = anchor x 1.6^era (600 / 960 / 1,536 / 2,458 against 600 / 1,320 / 2,904 / 6,389), everything else identical (A 2.2 / B 1.5, era-0 inputs x1.2 with the ladder anchored on it, ai_value 1,000x3^era, divisor 0.000125, the 10.75 defines, the 24-month bar, the era-rule canon's structure). WHY 1.6: a straight log interpolation of the two measured lifted A-2.2 books (C 1 -> 2.10x, C 2.2 -> 0.65x) lands GDP 1.0x at C ~1.65. NEXT: bisect on the result (above the GDP target band -> C 1.9; below -> C 1.3), one more bisection, then the lift (x1.3) at the found C.

_arms.canon-c16-in12: {kind: config, config: config/mod_config.canon-c16-in12.json} - generated 2026-09-14 by make_ab_config --cost-ratio 1.6 (the flag added the same day; the lint reads _ab.cost_ratio); the regenerated a22-in12 book is byte-identical to the committed one apart from stamps; dry-run built clean.

_delta: Against canon-je24-a22-in12 (F113, n=3): the cost slope 1.6^era in place of 2.2^era - one lever. Against canon-flat-in12 (F110) and canon-flat-in12-a19: the cost slope in place of flat cost, and A 2.2 (vs 1.9 for a19).

_predictions.gdp: world GDP 0.8-1.2x the vanilla n=16 median at 1935 (point ~1.0x). The early dip: 1860 at 0.80-0.95x vanilla's run 1 (a22-in12 0.92, a16 0.86, F110 1.08); the realignment is what the frontier's cheaper capital buys after 1880. Failure modes: above 1.2x means the explosive regime reaches C 1.6 (next: C 1.9); below 0.8x means the frontier is still too scarce (next: C 1.3).
_predictions.workers: productive workers per capita 0.65-0.85x vanilla (a22-in12 0.55, F110 1.23) - inside or just above the rule's target band 0.55-0.72; peasants per capita ABOVE vanilla's 7.5% at 1935 in most majors (the depeasantation reading, per major from the summaries)
_predictions.obsolescence: rung-0 staffing 25-45% at 1935 (a22-in12 57%, F110 18%), the era-0 staffed-level count FALLING 1900->1935, stale payback over 30 y; below-best 30-38%
_predictions.capital_prices: pools 0.3-0.7 of a year's world GDP (a22-in12 0.26, F110 2.28); the tiered goods' British prices 0.7-0.9x vanilla's; tiered levels 12,000-25,000 (a22-in12 ~6,500, vanilla 21,971, F110 51,893)
_predictions.perf: row P total within +10% of vanilla's median play time (a19 +9-12%: a bigger world is slower)

_alignment: THE 2+1 RULE (user-ruled 2026-09-14, F114): after run 2, `node tools/testbed/ledger/alignment_check.mjs --arm <session>:canon-c16-in12` - two criteria at 1935 vs the vanilla per-run median, five bands each, a pair fails an axis only in different bands AND >= 0.15 (GDP) / >= 0.10 (workers) apart. DIVERGENT => one more run of this config as its own one-run schedule, the reading the median of three. No obsolescence criterion; rung-0 staffing / payback / below-best are verdict flags.
_comparison: vanilla n=16 (20260821_131149) for every ratio; canon-je24-a22-in12 (F113) is the one-lever baseline; canon-flat-in12 (F110) and canon-flat-in12-a19 (its own finding) the flat-cost end.
_watch: every run ~5 min in: mod marker, version, this run's error window by position, clock (batch_heartbeat.sh at each wake)

first run: first_run_decomp at 1900/1935, rung margins by era at 1840/1900/1935 (scratchpad rung_margins.mjs), pools / unemployment / peasants (world_labour.mjs), queue_mix; the 1860 dip against vanilla's run 1
post-run: alignment_check.mjs, preflight -Session, VERDICT.md, SESSION_VERDICTS row, FINDINGS, the ledger (one configuration per report)
_cost: 2 x 1836->1936 ~ 2 x 2h20-3h00 ~ 5-6 h, plus a third run of the same on divergence (the rule passes ~40-47% of this family's pairs, so the third run is likely).
_caveats: n=2 by design; the alignment tool decides on the third.

Launch ONLY through tools/testbed/launch_detached.ps1 CALLED DIRECTLY from the PowerShell tool (landmine L30); the STOP file must be absent; the five-minute smoke check on EVERY run; never interleave configs.
